visual: Teardrop wisp shape, half its body bathed in warm amber-white, half in cool ashen grey; the divide is not a clean line but a flickering blurred edge; tiny trailing tail of mist.
hook: A kin visibly fighting its own hollowing — warm and dark at once, genuinely moving.

name: Wispwane
concept: A wisp caught between the Skyweave and the Hollowing — half its body radiates pale golden light, the other half swirls with cold dark vapour. It is the living boundary between what Vesperholm was and what it is becoming. Neither side has won yet.
visual: Elongated wisp with a clear left/right split: the light half is warm ivory-gold with a faint inner shimmer; the dark half is deep indigo-void with null-mist tendrils; the division is a crackling seam of sparks.
signature_idea: Waning Pulse — hits as both Dark and Light simultaneously; deals reduced damage but cannot be fully resisted by either type
hook: The one kin that embodies the whole game's conflict in its body — kids will argue about whether it's dark or light.

name: Liminalux
concept: The resolved form of a wisp that survived the Hollowing's full pull and did not fall entirely dark — nor entirely light. It exists as a stable chimera, its body a sphere of coexisting radiance and void. Its presence calms both lit and hollow kin.
visual: Large orb-being, one hemisphere bright bone-white with a golden core, the other deep void-black with a violet inner light; a belt of crackling silver sparks rings the equator; two long pale tendrils drift like arms.
signature_idea: Equilibrium — raises own SpA and SpD simultaneously; also halves the opponent's most recent type modifier
hook: A kin that resolved the game's central conflict in its own body — the reward for finding it feels earned.

name: Mothdim
concept: A small grey moth whose wing-eyes were once luminous but are now flat and lightless — ashen circles where the glow used to be. It flutters through coldfog seeking the warmth it can no longer feel.
visual: Coin-sized moth, chalk-grey wings with faded circular eye-markings that hold no light; segmented dusty body, antennae curled downward; at 16px reads as a tiny winged oval.
hook: A moth whose eye-spots have gone dark — instantly melancholy, immediately recognisable.

name: Nullmoth
concept: A palm-sized moth draped in velvet-grey wings that shed fine null-dust — a powder that drains faint light sources on contact. Its dead lantern marking on each hindwing is unmistakable.
visual: Slate-grey wings with a stylised snuffed-lantern motif on each hindwing — the lantern arch and pane visible but the flame glyph hollow; body wrapped in soft ashen fuzz; dull violet undersides.
signature_idea: Null Dust — entry hazard that dims incoming Light-type moves for 3 turns
hook: The snuffed-lantern wing pattern is the emblem of the Coldfog Marches — instantly iconic.

name: Voidmantle
concept: A large, crepuscular moth whose wingspan fills a doorway. Its wings are so saturated with null-dust that they absorb the ambient glow from nearby kin, leaving a sphere of unnatural dark around it. An apex predator of light.
visual: Huge moth, wings deep charcoal edged in ghostly silver-white trim; six dead-lantern symbols across both wings; a feathered thorax like a burial shroud; compound eyes a milky, sightless grey.
signature_idea: Shroud Drift — spreads Null Dust field, forces opponent switches on entry
hook: A moth that eats light itself — awe-inducing at the right stage of the game.

name: Wispwane
concept: A guttering will-o'-wisp of the Coldfog Marches — a Light kin slowly drained by the Hollowing, now barely half-lit; it drifts erratically, luring rivals toward the coldfog while leaking residual radiance.
visual: Small floating orb of pale light, but the glow is sickly and flickering; half its body fades into dark-grey shadow; a pained face barely visible in the dim half; dark mist trails from its underside; haunting and sad at 16px.
hook: A kin that is visibly sick — players feel an immediate urge to 'rescue' it, which is emotionally resonant.

name: Wisprestored
concept: When a Wispwane is loved and re-kindled, the Hollowing's taint burns away and it blazes back as a radiant wisp of pure light — joyful, fast, and full of a renewed warmth.
visual: A now-healthy glowing orb, bright amber-white, streaming a long comet-tail of light-motes; a beaming face visible in its core; no dark shadow remains; moves with joyful swooping arcs; reads as a blazing meteor-head at 48px.
signature_idea: Rekindle — restores 50% of the user's HP; if the user was affected by any status condition, it is cleansed and the user gets +1 to all stats for 2 turns.
hook: The kindling evolution IS the narrative — recovering a drained kin back to full brilliance is the game's whole theme in one line.

name: Cindersob
concept: A small creature shaped like a charred ember-hound pup — the hollowed remnant of a once-warm hearth companion. Its body is ash-black with faint orange cracks where embers still smoulder inside a hollowed chest.
visual: Small four-legged hound of black char, ribs faintly visible as orange-glow cracks; a wisp of cold smoke from a snuffed tail-flame; dull copper eyes; silhouette reads as a small dog at 16px.
hook: A puppy that is clearly the ghost of a warm hearth-dog — heartbreaking and immediately sympathetic.

name: Embergone
concept: The snuffed final form of a proud ember-kin lineage — a tall hound whose once-brilliant coat is reduced to cracked obsidian shot through with dying ember veins. It runs in silence, trailing no warmth. The hollow in its chest is the shape of a lost flame.
visual: Lean upright hound, obsidian-black body with orange-amber hairline cracks radiating from a dark chest hollow; ears still flame-tapered but dull copper; tail a dead cinder-stump; eyes a faint dying coal-glow.
signature_idea: Cinder Grief — special Dark move that deals bonus damage equal to missing ember-warmth; ignores type resistances on a 'remembered fire' mechanic flavour
hook: Named for what it lost — kids will feel the tragedy in the name before reading a word of the dex entry.

name: Whorlix
concept: A storm-husk kin that drifted in from the Coldfog Marches: a hollow shell of compressed dark air and residual lightning, still discharging sporadically from inside an empty void-core.
visual: Tall hollow silhouette like a funnel-cloud with a gap where the centre should be, dark ink-purple swirling walls faintly lit by trapped lightning, jagged trailing tendrils; uneasy void-shape at 48px.
signature_idea: Void Static — drains opponent's PP on the moves they use most frequently; applies confusion.
hook: A storm made of nothing — the Hollowing's mark on electricity, eerie and unforgettable.

name: Nullhusk
concept: The charged husk of the Hollowfen Stillworks — a derelict Hollowing null-works set-piece in Coldfog Marches. Once a thunderhead-kin captured and drained into a null-lantern to power the Stillworks machinery, Nullhusk has become something new: a storm-shaped void that still generates electricity through pure muscle memory while the light it once had has been entirely eaten. It haunts the Stillworks' shattered null-lantern array, discharging arcs of dead-charged dark-storm energy into the rusted machinery. It does not know it has been emptied — it keeps generating, a habit that outlasted its soul.
visual: A thunderhead-bull silhouette rendered in absolute void: the body outline is a deep storm-shape filled with dark non-light, negative-space body, but from it leak erratic arcs of dead-current in a sickly violet-grey that never quite reaches the warmth of true storm-blue. The eyes are empty null-lantern apertures — circular, glass-cold, unlit. The horns still crackle with charge. Reads as something that was majestic and is now entirely hollow.
signature_idea: Dead Circuit — discharges all accumulated null-charge in a single catastrophic arc that deals Dark damage scaled to how many status conditions are on the field, then wipes all field effects including its own; a scorched-earth move that clears everything.
hook: The most haunting optional encounter in the game: a thunderstorm that has been hollowed out. Players will feel Còr's philosophy as something terrible and real through this one battle.

name: Cindervast
concept: The Drownlight Beacon sub-legendary — a vast shadow-whale that was once a Solar-type celestial guardian of the old beacon. The Hollowing snuffed its stored daylight entirely and refashioned it into a creature of pure null. It circles the beacon's foundations in the deep fog, singing a song at a frequency no living thing can hear.
visual: Enormous cetacean silhouette, deep void-black with faint silver constellation-marks still visible along its flanks (the ghost of what it was); fins trail null-mist; a crescent of anti-light glows where its blowhole was; awe-tier size.
signature_idea: Null Tide — the signature: a wave of void that hits the entire opposing side; drains one positive stat stage from each target; requires the Drownlight Beacon encounter to access
hook: A beacon-whale who once lit the coast, now the dark that extinguishes it — the most poignant creature in the dex.

name: Bogvast
concept: An enormous null-beast that has become part of the coldfog marshes themselves — its body encrusted with dead reed-stalks, snuffed lantern-frames, and darkened mineral deposits. Travelers have always assumed it was a piece of geography. It moves only when something enters its null-field.
visual: Vast tortoise-like creature, entirely hidden beneath an shell of snuffed lanterns, dead reeds, and null-stone; only the deep void-dark eyes and four pillar-legs betray it as alive; its back looks like a section of blighted marsh terrain.
signature_idea: Stillmarch — on entry, sets a terrain field that reduces all opponents' Speed by one stage per turn spent in battle; the 'being slowly swallowed by the marsh' feeling
hook: An apex creature that IS the coldfog marsh — players who didn't look carefully will be stunned when it moves.

name: Skyweavelet
concept: A mote of the Skyweave itself given semi-sapient form — a thread-sprite that weaves small patches of the celestial fabric back together wherever the Hollowing has frayed it, arriving at the Crossroads ahead of each constellation relight.
visual: Tiny humanoid woven entirely from luminous thread; body is a loose tangle of glowing filaments in soft cyan, gold and white; legs and arms are thread-loops; a face of two bright white dots in a small thread-loop oval; carries a spool of golden thread on one wrist; whimsical and unique at 16px.
signature_idea: Skyweave Stitch — removes all field hazards from both sides of the battlefield AND prevents hazards being placed on the ally's side for 2 turns; if used before a relit-area encounter it gives the whole party +5% exp.
hook: It is literally mending the sky — the game's lore made playable in a tiny, charming form. Players who love the story will feel this kin IS the journey.

name: Lampling
concept: The beloved mascot of Vesper Crossroads — a sentient vesperlamp kin that has been glowing at the crossroads inn for longer than anyone can remember. It welcomes every weary traveller with a warm amber light and an unhurried tilt of its brass hood.
visual: Squat, teardrop-shaped body of burnished brass, a round glass-chimney belly filled with warm amber glow; two small mitten-like hands grip the base; tiny curled feet; a brass hood sits slightly askew like a jaunty cap; warm cream light pools at its base; instantly iconic at 32px — fat oval + hat silhouette.
signature_idea: Heartlight — sets a persistent healing field for 4 turns (allies recover 1/8 HP each turn) and clears all party status conditions on use.
hook: It IS the crossroads — the mascot every player will bond with on their first visit. A hug in kin form.

name: Keylumen
concept: The Keystar-kin. At the heart of the Umbral Spire, sealed within the Ninth Lantern, rests the being that the old Vesperholm star-tenders simply called the First Light — the original anchor of the Keystar, the central star without which no other constellation can hold. Keylumen is not a creature that chose to be a star: it is a star that chose to become a creature, once, long ago, because it was curious about the world below. It is vast and tender and utterly singular. When the Hollowing's Great Null reaches toward the Keystar, Keylumen rises from within the darkened lantern — not to fight, but to remember. And in remembering, it outshines everything around it. Scripted encounter; cannot be encountered in the wild.
visual: A tall, upright cervine figure — like a great stag, but made entirely of woven starlight. No hard edges: the silhouette blooms and shifts like a constellation drawing. The body is a deep midnight-blue field shot through with dense white-gold star-points; the antlers are open latticework of pure light, each tip a true star. The eyes are two full-disc pupils of warm solar gold. At rest it looks like a lantern-constellation stepped down from the sky. In battle it pulses with ever-brightening rings of diamond-cyan. The art reads iconic at every sprite size.
signature_idea: Keylight — the Keystar flares through the user, striking all opposing kin simultaneously with pure Light damage that ignores resistances and then leaving a Radiance field that heals the user's side each turn for three turns; the move that relights the sky.
hook: Keylumen is the answer to the whole game's question. Catching it feels not like a victory but like being trusted.

name: Nullmajor
concept: Warden Còr's drained final-boss kin — the embodiment of the Great Null, the shape that all the harvested light takes when there is nowhere left to go. Nullmajor is not malicious. It is vast and sorrowful, the accumulated darkness of every snuffed lantern and every constellation dimmed by the Hollowing's null-lanterns. In battle at the Umbral Spire's peak, it does not attack: it absorbs. It pulls light from the air, from the player's kin, from the Skyweave Crown itself. To face it is to understand what Còr was trying to create — a world where the pain of losing light simply stops, because there is none left. Post-story, Còr releases it; it dissolves into the sky as dawn returns, becoming the last dark before morning.
visual: A colossal figure, roughly humanoid in silhouette — but hollow. The outline is a dense ink-black void rimmed with a faint cold-violet corona. Within the outline is not darkness but anti-light: a negative space where the battle background is inverted, as if the creature is a hole in the world. Còr's null-lantern floats at the centre of its chest, still lit with inverted cold-violet. The face is a smooth featureless oval of pure absence. No eyes. It is the saddest design in the game — it looks like grief given form.
signature_idea: Great Null — draws every Light-typed bonus, Radiance effect, and STAB boost from the field into itself, converting them to raw Dark power and unleashing them as a single devastating pulse that also lowers all enemy kin's Special Attack for two turns; the anti-dawn.
hook: The final boss that makes players feel the weight of the story's moral. Not hateable — heartbreaking. The memory of this fight is the one that lasts.

name: Dawnbrael
concept: The Dawn Legendary — the kin that was always there, sleeping beneath Dawnstead in a sealed reliquary of sunrise-stone, waiting for the day that never came. It is not a new creature: it is the oldest kin in Vesperholm, the guardian of the first dawn, placed there by the original star-tenders as a failsafe for a worst case they hoped would never arrive. When dawn finally returns and the Dawnstead reliquary opens, Dawnbrael emerges as a lion-stag blazing with actual sunlight — not stored, not remembered, but real. For the first time in the game, a kin casts hard-edged shadows behind it. It is the payoff for finishing everything.
visual: A lion-stag — lion's body with a stag's great antlers — made of and wreathed in actual sunlight. The coat is amber-to-white radiance, the mane a full halo of solar corona arcs in diamond-cyan and fire-orange. The antlers are molten gold with sun-flare tips, casting hard shadows in every direction. Eyes are two full solar discs: white-hot centres with amber halos. In the post-game palette of true daylight colours, it reads as a creature from a different, brighter world — because it is.
signature_idea: First Dawn — summons a true solar field that replaces all weather effects, boosts every Solar- and Light-typed move by ×1.5 for five turns, and deals full-power physical Solar damage to the target with a follow-through Light pulse that hits every remaining opponent at half power; the move the game was building toward.
hook: The reward for completing the journey. The moment Dawnbrael steps into real sunlight for the first time, the game earns everything it promised.
